## Appearance

Agatha Sowerby is a stout female with a heavy body weighing two hundred pounds. Her physical frame results in a gait that is a perpetual waddle, and she has gentle, aged arms.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Agatha Sowerby Is Properly Horrified P31](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0031), [v1 CHAPTER XXXVIII. ## Personality

A pious Christian woman who is deeply devout and actively involved in religious matters, she is known for her cheerful, gentle, and motherly nature. She is exceptionally kind-hearted and industrious, showing remarkable compassion and endurance as a caregiver while remaining an avid dressmaker. At the same time, she is an opinionated, candid, and often meddlesome talker who takes great pride in voicing her firm beliefs without partiality. Her severe, strict, and domineering tendencies lead her to actively train those around her and criticize others, including young housekeepers and college graduates. Although observant and possessed of great foresight, she can be pessimistic, lacking in delicacy, and burdened with a sense of responsibility for every concern of church and state. Her strong convictions also make her a passionate partisan who holds a bias against [Yankees](../codex/factions.md#yankee) and firmly opposes higher education for women.

## History

Mrs. Agatha Sowerby was raised on St. Brendan's [Island](../codex/places.md#brendan-s-island), having married by the age of eighteen and gone on to raise ten children while suffering the loss of two. Her husband had previously worked for a [Boston](../codex/places.md#boston) boss who cheated him out of ten dollars. She initially expressed strong doubts when [Obed Abernethy](../character/obed-abernethy.md) set out to adopt an orphan from [Nova Scotia](../codex/places.md#nova-scotia), and she later insulted the young Nell's plain appearance and red hair. After [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) delivered a humble apology at her house, Agatha readily forgave her. When [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) later smashed a slate over a boy's head at school, Agatha advised [Thirza Abernethy](../character/thirza-abernethy.md) to let the girl rest at home until her temper cooled. She assisted [Obed](../character/obed-abernethy.md) with purchasing fabric and sewing a stylish gown with fashionable puffed sleeves for [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md), and she later brought news that [Hugh Carrow](../character/hugh-carrow.md) had withdrawn his application for the local teaching post so [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) could take it. Following the death of her husband [Thomas](../character/thomas-sowerby.md), Agatha was invited by [Thirza](../character/thirza-abernethy.md) to move into [Grey Shutters](../codex/places.md#grey-shutters) so [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) could attend college. While living there, she managed household matters, including sending [Robin](../character/robin-farrow.md) to bed without dinner for lying and writing letters to [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) at [Wexcombe](../codex/places.md#wexcombe-college). She continued living at [Grey Shutters](../codex/places.md#grey-shutters) alongside [Thirza](../character/thirza-abernethy.md), participating in preparations for [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) and Hugh's eventual wedding, and later joined the couple for a [Christmas](../codex/places.md#merry-christmas) dinner celebration at [Seven Gulls](../codex/places.md#seven-gulls).

## Quotes

> "However, I had a bit of a scare that you might not be, seeing Obed head out earlier today. My thought was that perhaps he was heading to the doctor’s office."
>
> — Agatha Sowerby — [v1 CHAPTER I. Mrs. Agatha Sowerby Is Surprised P14](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0014)

> "I simply reckon she has succeeded, and I would certainly not hold back from stating as much. You bring honor to your companions, Nell, indeed you do, and every one of us is proud of you."
>
> — Agatha Sowerby — [v1 CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out P48](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0048)

> "I’m not aware of it. My assumption is that your teaching will take place directly here in Brierley. You have been selected by the trustees to receive the school."
>
> — Agatha Sowerby — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVIII. The Bend in the Road P36](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0036)

> "While I was returning from Delford today, Mr. Pettifer was seen by me driving your Jersey from his oats. It appeared to me that he was quite furious. Was a big fuss made by him?"
>
> — Agatha Sowerby — [v2 I An Irate Neighbor P38](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0038)

> "That is the truth, I had not seen her appear so agreeable previously. Ah, over that poor old woman, not many tears were wept. To be free of her brings gratitude to the Elisha Ducketts, and I am unable to say that I fault them in the least."
>
> — Agatha Sowerby — [v3 ch.Evening P11](../source/v03-c28.md#nw-v03-c28-p0011)

## Relationships

### [Nell Harcourt](../character/nell-harcourt.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/agatha-sowerby--nell-harcourt.md)

Agatha initially got off to a hostile start with [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) after rudely mocking the girl's plain appearance and red hair, provoking [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) into a violent temper. However, the feud ended after [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) brought herself to deliver a dramatic apology at Agatha's house, where Agatha forgave her and offered encouraging words about her hair. Agatha later offered advice to help manage Nell's schooling troubles, recommending that the girl be allowed to rest at home after an outburst in class.

### [Thirza Abernethy](../character/thirza-abernethy.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/agatha-sowerby--thirza-abernethy.md)

Agatha and [Thirza](../character/thirza-abernethy.md) are longstanding friends and neighbors who regularly visit each other's homes to trade gossip and discuss household matters. Although Agatha often offers unsolicited warnings and doubts regarding Thirza's domestic decisions, [Thirza](../character/thirza-abernethy.md) continues to turn to Agatha for advice when handling difficult situations. Following the death of Agatha's husband, [Thirza](../character/thirza-abernethy.md) proposes inviting the widowed Agatha to move into [Grey Shutters](../codex/places.md#grey-shutters).
